title: House Prices: Advanced Regression Techniques (stacking / ensemble project writeup)
why_relevant: Describes a strong ensemble/stacking approach (XGBoost, LightGBM, Lasso/ElasticNet) tailored to this exact competition and dataset shape.
extracted_technique: Vertical stacking / blending of linear models + GBDTs; skew transforms + one-hot encoding; careful preprocessing and ensembling for higher leaderboard accuracy.
query: Kaggle House Prices Advanced Regression Techniques winning solution LightGBM XGBoost CatBoost blend RMSE 0.06
takeaway: A high-performing recipe is to log-transform the target, handle missingness carefully, correct skew in numerics, and blend/stack diverse regressors (regularized linear + boosting). Use strict CV and OOF predictions to avoid leakage.

title: Stacked Regressions : Top 4% on LeaderBoard (Serigne)
why_relevant: Widely-cited canonical pipeline for this competition; informs a reproducible stacking template and common feature-prep steps used by strong community baselines.
extracted_technique: OOF-based stacking of Lasso/ElasticNet/KernelRidge/GBR with XGBoost/LightGBM; skew correction (Box-Cox-like) and robust preprocessing; final blend from OOF.
query: kaggle serigne stacked regressions top 4 on leaderboard
takeaway: Even if you modernize the tooling, the core idea remains: build diverse base learners, generate leak-free OOF predictions, then train a simple meta-model or weighted blend for a robust accuracy jump.

title: LightGBM Advanced Topics (missing values + categorical feature support)
why_relevant: Primary documentation clarifying how LightGBM treats missing values by default and how integer-encoded categorical features are handled, informing safe preprocessing choices.
extracted_technique: Rely on LightGBM missing-value handling; optionally use integer-coded categoricals with `categorical_feature` rather than one-hot for some pipelines; keep negative codes as missing.
query: LightGBM documentation categorical handling missing values one-hot vs categorical_feature
takeaway: LightGBM can handle NaNs natively and supports categorical splits with integer-encoded categoricals; this enables a high-capacity model without exploding one-hot dimensionality, but encoding must remain leak-free (fit on train folds only).

title: XGBoost Tree Methods (including gpu_hist)
why_relevant: Primary documentation for selecting GPU-accelerated training (`gpu_hist`) and understanding tradeoffs vs CPU histogram methods, enabling longer schedules on GPU.
extracted_technique: Use `tree_method=gpu_hist` for GPU training; tune `max_bin`, depth, subsampling; use early stopping on fold validation sets.
takeaway: GPU histogram training makes repeated CV/seed ensembling feasible. Prefer gpu_hist with early stopping and conservative regularization to reduce overfitting on small tabular data.

title: CatBoost processing unit settings (task_type, devices)
why_relevant: Primary documentation for enabling CatBoost GPU training and selecting GPU devices; supports a diverse model in the ensemble with strong categorical handling.
extracted_technique: Set `task_type='GPU'` and optionally `devices='0'`; combine with early stopping and categorical feature indices for robust performance.
query: CatBoost GPU training documentation task_type GPU
takeaway: CatBoost can be a strong complementary learner in a GBDT ensemble; GPU mode speeds up CV and helps justify multi-seed training while keeping the same algorithm across local_gpu and kaggle_gpu.
